body: Hub hello: a one-line check that a new seat reads its config and its memory. Drawer/hub-hello.py prints the hub display name from harness.toml and the count of open tasks in mem, then exits 0. It needs no product checkout, no network and no OpenAI key.
title: Hub hello

body: Plain short words beat clever ones in every string a user reads.
Each user action gets a clear answer: a message, a change on screen or an exit code, never silence.
Cut a feature before it ships half done: a small finished thing beats a large rough one.

hub-hello: add Drawer/hub-hello.py, which prints one line with the hub display name from harness.toml and the open task count from mem, and its unittest test Drawer/test_hub_hello.py. Skills: harness. Spec: state none written, read only; life a new script and test, nothing removed; breaks no harness.toml key or an empty mem prints the line with 0, a missing mem file exits 0 with count 0; neighbours reads harness.toml through Drawer/harness_config.py and mem through Drawer/mem/mem.py, no network, no OpenAI key; data the test runs on a temp mem db with a known task count; proof .venv/bin/python -B -m unittest Drawer/test_hub_hello.py green and the ship smoke; sees a dev reads one line like <name>: <n> open tasks; keeps no change to mem, harness_config or other scripts. Why: a new seat has no quick check that config and memory both read, and a first task should need no product checkout. Done when: the script prints one line and exits 0 on a fresh clone with no OpenAI key, and its test (a unittest.TestCase file, as every hub test is) passes under python -B -m unittest.
title: hub-hello
